title: A Protocol for the Signal
premise: Felix Thornbury, a nonbinary insurance investigator who insures the long-haul relay ships crossing the silent gulf between two estranged human fleets, intercepts a distress call in Old Meridian—a language extinct since the fleets' founding schism. The signal comes from a reactor station on the border, and its countdown will trigger war if it reaches zero. To stop it, Felix must impersonate a dead diplomat whose identity they've secretly inherited, sustaining one lie that keeps both fleets from firing while falling in love with Commander Sefa Okonkwo, the woman assigned to verify them. In the end Felix broadcasts the truth—their own forged identity and the station's real message of reconciliation—choosing exposure over duty; the lie collapses, but the truth holds the peace, and Felix survives the countdown stripped of every name except their own.
about_author: Ines Voss is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years listening to frequencies no one else answered before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted lighthouse on the Baltic coast, where she insists the static still says things.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. We meet Felix mid-investigation aboard the relay ship Perpetual Ledger, cataloging an 'impossible accident' that was really sabotage. Establishes the silent two-fleet cold war, Felix's talent for invisibility, and their quiet grief over an extinct language they study in secret. Emotional beat: competent loneliness.

chapters.title: A Voice in Dead Air
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Alone on night watch, Felix intercepts a distress signal in Old Meridian—the language of the unified fleet before the schism. No one else can read it. They decode enough to learn it's a countdown, not a plea. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of being uniquely needed.

chapters.title: Chain of Custody
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Commander Sefa Okonkwo is ordered to escort the investigator to the border station and quietly determine whether they're a spy. She finds Felix's file suspiciously clean—and one sealed record she isn't cleared to open. Emotional beat: professional suspicion sharpening into fascination.

chapters.title: The Dead Diplomat
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the border station, Felix discovers the distress beacon is keyed to Ambassador Ilse Varga—dead for thirty years—whose identity documents Felix has carried since a previous case went wrong. The countdown accelerates. To access the reactor core, Felix must become Varga. Emotional beat: the first deliberate step into the lie.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Room
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A joint verification hearing convenes; both fleets' officers interrogate 'Ambassador Varga.' Felix performs flawlessly while Sefa watches for cracks. Privately, Sefa confronts Felix with the sealed record—and chooses, for now, not to open it. Emotional beat: complicity disguised as mercy.

chapters.title: What the Reactor Remembers
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Descending into the station, Sefa learns the reactor is a broadcast array built by the pre-schism generation, programmed to transmit a reconciliation message the founders suppressed. The countdown isn't a weapon—it's a deadline someone set to force the truth out. Emotional beat: duty beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Both fleets mobilize as the countdown nears zero; only 'Varga' can stand between them. Felix and Sefa, working through the nights, cross from alliance into love neither will name. Felix realizes the lie keeping the fleets apart is also keeping them together. Emotional beat: tenderness inside a ticking clock.

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A rival officer opens the sealed record: Felix Thornbury is not Ilse Varga. Sefa must arrest them or help them. Both fleets' guns track the station. Sefa burns her own career, deleting the evidence and standing beside Felix instead. Emotional beat: love choosing itself over duty.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With minutes left, Felix abandons the Varga mask entirely and broadcasts in Old Meridian—their own voice, their own confession, and the founders' suppressed message decoded aloud. The fleets hold fire, transfixed by a language that remembers them as one people. The reactor reaches zero. Emotional beat: naked truth at maximum risk.

chapters.title: A Protocol for the Signal
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The transmission completes: not destruction but the founders' handshake protocol, finally delivered. Courts convene; Felix loses everything forged and keeps everything real—including Sefa, reassigned to the new joint relay. Felix signs their own name for the first time in years. Emotional beat: quiet, earned arrival.
